learning_goal: Point to every named part of the humerus on the bone, and say which nerve is at risk at each of the four places it commonly breaks.

structures.name: right humerus
structures.label: Humerus
structures.narration: One bone from shoulder to elbow. A rounded head above, a triangular shaft, and a wide flattened end below.

structures.name: right scapula
structures.label: Scapula
structures.narration: Above, the head sits in the glenoid cavity of the scapula — a shallow socket, which is why the shoulder is mobile and dislocates.

structures.name: right radius
structures.label: Radius
structures.narration: Below, the head of the radius spins against the capitulum.

structures.name: right ulna
structures.label: Ulna
structures.narration: The trochlear notch of the ulna grips the trochlea — a hinge, so the elbow only flexes and extends.

structures.label: Head of humerus
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and the scapula, within the proximal 30% — the glenohumeral joint (gap 1.00 mm); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: Faces up, back and medially into the glenoid. The narrow line round its rim is the anatomical neck.

structures.label: Greater tubercle
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the most lateral point of the proximal 12% of the bone, measured on the mesh (14.1 mm lateral of the shaft axis); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The lateral bump. Three cuff muscles land here: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor.

structures.label: Lesser tubercle
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and subscapularis (gap 0.09 mm); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The smaller bump in front. Subscapularis is the only muscle that reaches it.

structures.label: Intertubercular groove
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and the long head of biceps (gap 0.39 mm); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The gutter between the two tubercles. The long head of biceps runs down it, and three muscles attach on its lips — a lady between two majors.

structures.label: Surgical neck
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the narrowest level in the 10% of bone directly below the lowest tubercle — 28.8 mm wide against a 21.1 mm mid-shaft (Z-fraction 0.816); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: Where the flared top narrows into shaft — and the common fracture site in the elderly. The axillary nerve wraps round here, so a break can paralyse deltoid and numb the badge patch on the shoulder.

structures.label: Deltoid tuberosity
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and deltoid, restricted to the middle of the shaft (gap 0.75 mm, 13.2 mm off the shaft axis); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: A rough V on the lateral shaft, halfway down. Deltoid ends here.

structures.label: Radial groove
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: midpoint between the humeral contact of the lateral head of triceps (which arises above the groove, gap 0.30 mm) and that of the medial head (which arises below it, gap 0.40 mm), snapped back onto the bone (4.61 mm); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: A shallow spiral on the back of the shaft. The radial nerve and profunda brachii artery lie in it — a mid-shaft fracture here gives wrist drop.

structures.label: Supracondylar region
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the most ANTERIOR point of the bone within the slab z:0.10-0.25 — the front of the distal shaft, just above the epicondylar flare (Z-fraction 0.101, against 0.066 for the medial and 0.081 for the lateral epicondyle); 173 vertices considered; see tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA23130 --extreme -y --slab z:0.10,0.25
structures.narration: The flattened neck of bone just above the two epicondyles, and the commonest fracture site in a child. The brachial artery and the median nerve lie together on the front of it. The lower fragment tilts backwards and the sharp front edge of the upper fragment is driven forwards into both.

structures.label: Medial epicondyle
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the most medial point of the distal 12% of the bone (33.0 mm from the centre of the distal end); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The prominent medial bump — the common flexor origin. The ulnar nerve runs in a groove behind it, which is why knocking it tingles the little finger.

structures.label: Lateral epicondyle
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the most lateral point of the distal 12% of the bone (31.0 mm from the centre of the distal end); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The smaller lateral bump — the common extensor origin. Overuse of those tendons is tennis elbow.

structures.label: Trochlea
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and the ulna, within the distal 15% — the humero-ulnar joint (gap 0.62 mm); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The medial pulley. It grips the trochlear notch of the ulna and makes the elbow a hinge.

structures.label: Capitulum
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and the radius, within the distal 15% — the radiocapitellar joint (gap 4.85 mm, the widest of the set); see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The lateral ball. The head of the radius spins on it during pronation and supination.

views.title: See it in the body
views.narration: The humerus runs from the glenoid of the scapula down to the radius and ulna. Ball joint above, hinge below.

views.title: The top end
views.narration: Head, then two tubercles with the groove between them, then the surgical neck where the flare ends. Learn them in that order and the muscle attachments follow.

views.title: Turn it round: the shaft
views.narration: From behind: the deltoid tuberosity on the lateral side and the radial groove spiralling across the back.

views.title: Cut across the shaft
views.narration: Slide the cut down the bone. The shaft is a tube of compact bone round a marrow cavity, and it turns from round at the top to triangular lower down.

views.title: The bottom end
views.narration: Two epicondyles for muscle, two articular surfaces for bone. Trochlea to the ulna, capitulum to the radius — medial to medial, lateral to lateral.

views.title: The radial nerve's route
views.narration: The radial nerve leaves the axilla, crosses the back of the shaft in its groove, then passes in front of the lateral epicondyle. It is pinned to the bone in that groove, which is exactly why a mid-shaft fracture drops the wrist.

views.title: Break it here, lose that nerve
views.narration: Four fracture sites, four nerves, from the top down. Surgical neck takes the axillary nerve. Mid-shaft, in the radial groove, takes the radial. The supracondylar region takes the median nerve — and the brachial artery with it, which is the one that costs a hand. Medial epicondyle takes the ulnar. Say the site, then say the nerve.

provenance.author: task
provenance.corrected_by: human review — the task audit signed this scene while an error remained

gaps: Every named part of the humerus is a landmark anchor, because the catalog's smallest unit is the whole bone — there is no separate mesh for a tubercle, a groove or an epicondyle. Each anchor was measured on the mesh by tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs and carries its definition and its measurement in calibrated_by. All stay status:"needs-review" until a human has looked at them once.
The capitulum anchor has the largest contact gap of the set (4.85 mm to the radial head) because the joint space is wide there on the decimated meshes. It is the one anchor most worth a human eye.

The surgical neck is a short region rather than a point, and the anatomical neck is a line round the head that no measurement here isolates; both are taught in narration on the nearest measured anchor.

No nerve meshes exist in the catalog, so the radial nerve is traced as a concept along bony waypoints rather than shown as a structure. The axillary, median and ulnar nerves are named in narration only. Re-searched 2026-08-28 under nerve, nervus, median, ulnar, radial and axillary: nothing.

The brachial artery is named in the supracondylar narration and is not on screen: the catalog holds no upper-limb artery distal to the subclavian (re-searched 2026-08-28 for brachial, profunda, collateral, recurrent, radial artery and ulnar artery — the whole limb returns nothing). The vessel is described rather than shown, and gross__arm__brachial-artery teaches it as a diagram for the same reason.

The supracondylar region was measured on 2026-08-28 during the audit, to settle a contradiction: the learning goal promised four fracture sites, beat 7 delivered three, and gross__arm__median-ulnar-radial-nerves deferred to a fourth that had never been authored. It is a region rather than a point, so it is anchored at the most anterior point of the distal shaft above the epicondylar flare — the surface the artery and the median nerve actually lie on — and stays needs-review like the rest of the set.
